sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 46.6% a year from $6.91 billion in FY2017 to $215.9 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F211].
The path was not smooth: revenue fell 6.8% in FY2020 and was flat in FY2023, then jumped 125.9% in FY2024 and 114.2% in FY2025 [D130][D284][D338][D393].
The FY2024 step change came from Data Center revenue up 217% on Hopper GPU shipments for LLM training and inference [P23][P25].
FY2026 growth of 65.5% was driven by Blackwell data center compute and networking, with networking revenue up 142% [D448][P8][P10].
Data Center was 89.7% of FY2026 revenue and contributed 60.2pp of the 65.5% growth [D620][D622][D448].
Within it, Compute contributed 46.1pp and Networking 14.1pp in FY2026 [D629][D636].
Gaming, once 56.8% of revenue in FY2018, was 7.4% in FY2026 and added only 3.6pp [D637][D659][D661].
Operating income grew 60.1% against revenue growth of 65.5%, so incremental operating margin was 57.3% [D449][D448][D475].
Diluted EPS rose 66.7% in FY2026, slightly ahead of net income growth of 64.7%, as the diluted share count fell 1.2% [D452][D450][D470].
Operating margin of 60.4% in FY2026 sits well above the 32.8% window median but below the 62.4% FY2025 high [F50][D813][D812].
Gross margin fell 3.9pp and was the main drag on operating margin, which slipped 2.0pp [D462][D463].
Compute & Networking operating income absorbed a $4.5 billion H20 excess inventory and purchase obligation charge in the first quarter of FY2026 [P7].
R&D rose 43.2% on a 29% increase in compensation and a 79% increase in compute and infrastructure, though it still added 1.3pp to margin [D466][P5][D478].
Net margin held at 55.6% despite the operating decline, helped by $11.1 billion of other income from unrealized equity gains including Intel [F70][X120][P3].
Operating cash flow of $102.7 billion was 0.86x net income in FY2026, below the 0.91x window high for free cash flow to net income [F100][F60][D435][D827].
Free cash flow of $96.7 billion was a 44.8% margin, against a 44.4% window median [F110][D432][D822].
Capex of $6.04 billion was 2.8% of revenue and 2.13x D&A, up from 1.74x a year earlier [F105][D431][D437][D382].
Inventory grew 112.3% and receivables 66.8%, both faster than revenue, lifting days inventory to 125 [D474][D473][D446].
Net cash fell to $2.14 billion, just 1.0% of revenue, from $34.7 billion a year earlier, though it still ranks in the 83rd percentile of six semis peers [D441][D442][D386][D844].
The drop came from $52.2 billion of investing outflows, driven by higher equity investment purchases and the Groq license agreement [F120][P1].
Buybacks and dividends of $41.1 billion absorbed 42.5% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 1.2% [D443][D444][D470].
Return on average equity was 101.5%, against a peer median of 20.3% [D447][D849].
Customer concentration is high: one direct customer was 22% and another 14% of FY2026 revenue, both mainly Compute & Networking [P6].
China revenue fell 21.4% in FY2026, subtracting 4.1pp from growth, and its share dropped to 9.1% from 19.2% [D545][D546][D544][D541].
The FY2023 Graphics decline of 25% [D754] was a one-year cyclical event, with Graphics revenue up 57.0% in FY2026 [D747], so it is not a persistent flag.
Product revenue members sum to 190% of consolidated FY2026 revenue because some are totals of others, so segment shares should not be added [R2].
Gross margin: a further move below the FY2026 71.1% would confirm cost pressure, while a return above the 75.0% FY2025 high would reverse it [F30][F29].
Net cash: a fall below the FY2026 $2.14 billion, driven by investing outflows, would signal the balance sheet is being consumed by equity stakes [D441].
China revenue: a further decline from the FY2026 $19.7 billion would extend the 4.1pp drag on growth [S24][D546].
